title: Residency declaration flow and Geo-Pin Operator UI
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Customers need an explicit, auditable way to declare and lock where tenant data is stored for Hosted API workloads (region pinning), change retention policies per-tenant, and obtain machine-readable evidence bundles for compliance reviews. Current controls are fragmented: region hints exist in provisioning, but there is no tenant-level declaration UI, no operator to lock/pin multiple routes, and evidence exports are manual.
background: We already have region routing primitives and residency metadata encoded at provisioning. Legal and enterprise customers have asked for: 1) a declarative residency 'declaration' they can sign/acknowledge, 2) a console operator to pin routes (api endpoints, embed generation) to preferred regions with fallback behavior, and 3) automated evidence bundles (signed manifests + logs) for audits. This ticket scopes the UX + API + evidence automation orchestration for tenant-level region pinning and retention declaration.
goals: Build a Residency Declaration UX where customers formally select required regions and retention classes and acknowledge SLA/constraints
Ship a Geo-Pin Operator in Console to pin specific API routes and model classes to regions with explicit fallback rules
Produce an automated evidence export containing signed residency manifests, policy change history, and access logs suitable for audit ingestion
Expose an API and CLI to read/write residency declarations for infra automation and contracts
non_goals: Global data-migration tooling (out of scope for this ticket)
Changing underlying routing heuristics or kernel-level scheduling (implements only policy layer)
On-prem private deployments (this is Hosted API scoped only)
acceptance_criteria: Console: Residency Declaration page that captures tenant's selected preferred region(s), retention profile (Short/Default/Long), and a signed acknowledgement
Console: Geo-Pin Operator flow that can pin specific API routes (pattern matching) to up to 3 regions and define a single ordered fallback list
API: POST/GET endpoints for residency declarations and geo-pin rules with RBAC checks documented in openapi spec
Evidence Export: One-click export that returns a timestamped, signed JSON bundle including declaration, pin rules, change history, and associated audit logs for the selected period
Auditability: All policy changes recorded in immutable audit log with who/when/why and export includes cryptographic signature metadata
E2E: Integration tests that assert pinned routes are routed to pinned regions in staging and fallback triggers if capacity is exhausted
tasks: Draft console wireframes and copy for declaration page (work with Design)
Define API contract and update openapi spec for residency endpoints (ENG + API infra)
Implement backend operator service that stores pin rules and exposes expirable signed manifests
Hook evidence export to audit log store and signer service
Add RBAC checks and admin-only UI controls
Add telemetry: policy change events, export events, and pin rule enforcement metrics
Run legal/infosec review on acknowledgement language and evidence artifacts
Create integration tests and a staging runbook for rollout
design_notes: Design should emphasize explicitness: customers must see visual confirmation of regions pinned, capacity/latency tradeoffs, and the fallback order. Use a multi-select chip UI for regions with an inline explainers modal. Include a read-only historical timeline for changes on the tenant page.
api_contract_summary: New endpoints: GET /v1/tenants/{id}/residency, POST /v1/tenants/{id}/residency, GET/POST /v1/tenants/{id}/geo-pin-rules, POST /v1/tenants/{id}/residency/export. Payloads include tenant_id, regions[], retention_profile, ack_signature, rules[]. RBAC role: tenancy_admin or organization_admin only.
evidence_format: Signed JSON bundle (UTF-8) containing metadata.json, declaration.json, rules.json, changelog.json, and logs.tar.gz link. Each bundle includes a signer_id and signature and a canonicalization hash for verification. Bundle S3 path and signed URL included in export response.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Design review and API spec approval
Week 1-2: Backend and API implementation in a feature branch; internal test harness
Week 3: Console UI implementation behind a feature flag; controlled staging test with 3 pilot tenants
Week 4: Legal/Compliance sign-off; enable evidence export for pilot tenants
Week 5: Gradual rollout to paid tenants; monitor telemetry and rollback plan
risks: Mis-declaration by tenants causing regulatory non-compliance - mitigated by clear copy and mandatory acknowledgement
Edge cases where a pinned region has zero capacity causing increased latency for fallback - mitigated by fallback ordering and capacity signals
Evidence export contains PII in logs - mitigated by scrub rules and retention window for exported logs
Operational complexity of managing signed manifests and key rotations - coordinate with security team
open_questions: Should we allow partial pins (route-level) for sub-resources like embeddings vs. text-generation?
Do we need region-level billing visibility tied to pins?
What retention class mapping should default for small tenants vs. enterprise tenants?
Signature format: do we adopt internal signer v2 or standard JWS for cross-org validation?
